signature: “M. FRIEDR / ICH. EHE / IN. NURNB / 1743”; master’s mark as on 1741.
dimensions: bo 10.8, be 134, le 3315, throat 44.5, mp entry 13.5, slide sec. exit 11.9, slide sec. le 2104, bell sec. le 1237, overlap 26, bell entry 13.5,
literature: Dérans 1995; Herbert 2004 [gives Stockhom MMF, and suggests it’s a typo from Waterhouse, for SMF--Stiftelsen Musikkulturen Främjande.
remarks: Tubular slide stays with Nuremberg-style floral pattern; eyelet for handle on lower stay, but handle is missing; Nuremberg- style floral pattern on slide stays (excellent condition), slide-bow has saddle with ring, zigzag pattern on saddle; bumper knob at bottom of slide bow; new tubing at beginning of neck pipe (perhaps alteration in pitch of instrument); 1 flat bell stay, with decoration identical to 1741, bell bow has saddle and ring; attached to saddle is base for finial but finial is missing; garland has four raised angel’s heads with wings; Nuremberg-style rim wire with leaf pattern; raised dots at top of garland. Examined by author 15 Aug 02. Part of a set with 1741-2 and 1743-2. Dérans 1995 mentions 3 trombones (descant or alto, tenor and bass) signed 1741 and 1743).” The same source mentions “1 original case for the trombone, brownpainted [sic] exterior and redpainted [sic] interior with blue velvet. The case is meant for 4 trombones, a whole family, but the smallest one is missing.”
